title: Meta to Build C$13 Billion Alberta Data Center, its First in Canada
source_used: The Energy Mix, 'Alberta Tribunal To Decide Whether Challenge To Meta Data Centre Can Proceed'
key_facts: Meta announced on 8 Jul 2026 that its first Canadian data centre, a $13 billion AI project in Sturgeon County near Edmonton, had won approval.
More than 125 people applied to challenge the county permit; an Alberta tribunal (LPRT) heard arguments on 13 Oct about who may appeal and whether the county misapplied its bylaw.
The project was a permitted use, so the bylaw allowed no public hearing or notice; plans were code-named Project Frost.
Power is to come from the Greenlight Electricity Centre at the same site; Meta bid on another company's grid allotment until the plant is ready in late 2030.
The county's lawyer argued only people within 3 km should have standing; residents' representative called that arbitrary.
The tribunal said it does not expect a decision on how to proceed for two to three weeks.
The county imposed 41 conditions on the permit.
quote_evidence: More than 125 people applied to challenge the permit.
The LPRT said it doesn't expect to reach a decision on how or whether to proceed with the appeal for two to three weeks.
why_it_matters_hint: The approval is old news, but the challenge shows how little say residents have over very large data centers.
event_date: Approval announced 8 Jul 2026; tribunal hearing 13 Oct 2026
notes: EnergyNow page (July 2026 article) returned no text; the story is the July announcement re-dated. Used The Energy Mix's 15 Oct report for the new development.
